verdict: REFUTED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by tuning
question: Every class refuted on this body so far was about RANK or BASIS. A near-random spectrum says the mass cannot be summarised by few DIRECTIONS; it says nothing about whether a few INDIVIDUAL weights carry disproportionate error. Sparsity is a different claim and was untested.
method: Bulk grouped affine plus a fraction s of weights kept as fp16, selected by ERROR MAGNITUDE after the bulk pass -- the weights the bulk codec got most wrong, which is the strongest form of the hypothesis. Index bytes counted at FULL width, ceil(log2(N)) = 25 bits per correction on a 3.1M-element tensor, plus 16 payload bits: 41 bits per repaired weight. No delta coding, no run-length, nothing needing its own decoder to be honest.
why_it_is_structural: At a matched 4.5 EBPW the sparse arm has NO CHOICE about its bulk. 4-bit grouped affine at group 64 already IS 4.500 EBPW, so every byte spent on corrections must be taken from the bulk, which means dropping to 3 bits. That costs a full bit on 97.4% of the weights to perfect 2.6% of them. The measured result is not close: top-1 0.6266 against the control's 0.8231 at 4.5, and 0.0557 against 0.5904 at 3.5. This does not depend on the index encoding -- a block-local 6-bit index would raise s from 2.6% to ~4.5% and the bulk would still have to fall to 3 bits, because the budget can only come from there.
unified_mechanism: Four classes have now failed on this body for ONE reason: low-rank, activation-aware low-rank, cross-layer shared basis, and sparse residual. Each looked for CONCENTRATION in a different basis -- the weight spectrum, the activation eigenbasis, a basis shared across layers, and individual weight magnitude -- and in every one the information is SPREAD. The single method that did win, error-compensating quantization, is the one that never looks for concentration at all: it does not try to find a small set to keep, it reallocates the error it is already forced to make.
reopen_condition: Sparse representation reopens only above a target EBPW where the bulk need not be reduced -- i.e. when the budget exceeds the bulk codec's own rate -- or on a specimen whose weight error IS concentrated (measurable in advance: top-k error mass vs a matched random control, which on this body is flat).
